build.#: The zena command: the host binary and the CLI module it runs.
build.#dependencies: `cascade: false` on build:module so dependents rerun only when out/zena.wasm's bytes change, and on precompile:module so the untracked .cwasm step stays out of downstream fingerprints.

build:binary.#: The host binary. Two scripts for one build: `build:cargo` declares no inputs, so wireit never calls it fresh and cargo is always consulted — cargo tracks its own inputs better than a `files` list could, and a no-op is a quarter of a second. This one names the binary cargo produced as an *input*, so its fingerprint changes exactly when the binary does, and that is what dependents inherit. `cascade: false` keeps `build:cargo`'s own fingerprint out: a script with no `files` is not `fullyTracked`, and wireit propagates that to everything downstream, where nothing can ever be fresh. Hashing the binary also makes freshness imply the binary exists, so a cache hit against an empty target dir cannot leave the scripts that run it failing with exit 127.

build:cargo.#: The repository's binary, without `--features bundled`. It embeds nothing built from Zena: in a repository it reads the CLI module and the standard library from disk (see CONTEXT.md), so it waits for no compiler and a Zena change never relinks it. Always runs; `build:binary` is what dependents read.

build:standalone.#: The zena command for use outside a repository: `--features bundled` embeds the standard library and the CLI module (out/stdlib_bundle.rs, from build:bundle-assets), and the build script fails without them. Nothing in the repository runs this binary, so `build` does not build it. It has its own target directory, so building it never replaces the binary every other script runs; the price is compiling wasmtime once more, the first time.

build:bundle-assets.#: Generates out/stdlib_bundle.rs from the standard library's sources and out/zena.wasm. bundle.zena is compiled and run on zena-run, which is what lets the zena command have one Rust build: the binary that embeds this bundle cannot also be the one that produces it.
build:bundle-assets.command: mkdir -p out && cd ../.. && ZENA_GC_RESERVE_MB=1536 ./target/release/zena-run --dir .::. --dir packages/stdlib/zena::/stdlib packages/zena-compiler/zena/out/cli.wasm packages/zena-cli/dev/bundle.zena -o packages/zena-cli/out/bundle.wasm && ./target/release/zena-run --dir .::. packages/zena-cli/out/bundle.wasm

build:module.#command: The compiler just built from source compiles the CLI module, run on zena-run with the preopens `zc` expects. It keeps its name section, like the compiler, so a trap in it names functions. Precompiling it is a separate script: it needs the zena command's binary, which is built from the bundle this module goes into.
build:module.command: mkdir -p out && cd ../.. && ZENA_GC_RESERVE_MB=1536 ZENA_DEBUG_NAMES=1 ./target/release/zena-run --dir .::. --dir packages/stdlib/zena::/stdlib packages/zena-compiler/zena/out/cli.wasm packages/zena-cli/zena/main.zena -o packages/zena-cli/out/zena.wasm

test.#: The Rust crates' own tests, and the command's tests, which run the built binary from Zena (tests/*_test.zena).

test:cargo.#command: --release reuses the dependency artifacts the build step produced instead of compiling wasmtime a second time in the dev profile. The features are build:cargo's, so the two share every artifact.

test:zena.#dependencies: build:cli without its fingerprint: workspace-errors_test.zena runs stage A as ZENA_COMPILER_WASM, so its bytes are an input. ../registry:test without its fingerprint, only so the two never run at once: each zena test held 5 to 7 GiB on CI's 16 GiB runner, and the two together ran it out of memory. The registry's own tests go first, since these run the registry end to end.

test:pds-js.#: zena pkg login and service auth against pds.js, which tests/pds-js/setup.mjs fetches. Not part of test, since it needs the network.

precompile:module.#: The CLI module's .cwasm, so the first zena commands do not race to run Cranelift on it. After the binary, because wasmtime's version is what decides whether a .cwasm can be loaded at all. Untracked so remote caches never save machine code built for one host CPU and restore it onto another; when out/zena.cwasm already loads on this host, `precompile` exits after deserializing it.
